hot.title: Embodied Turing Machines: Stateful Code for Robot Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: COAP represents scene state in code and uses a fixed task program to choose actions, check outcomes, and update its records. At test time, it uses camera images and robot measurements without a model service. On RoboDojo, it reaches 70.24% overall success, versus 31.38% for PhysicalRSI. Results are from simulation and depend on state measurement and code robustness.

hot.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
hot.summary: The authors train coding agents with groupwise grading, comparing attempts at the same task to add quality signals to binary test rewards. Online Groupwise Advantage Redistribution shifts positive credit toward higher-quality passing patches. MiMo-V2.6-Pro’s reported average pass-rate score across three sampled attempts rises from 58.4 to 72.6 on DeepSWE v1.1, but this mixed-task run does not isolate grading or compute effects.

hot.title: Recursive Self-Improvement through Multi-Agent Self-Supervision
hot.summary: MASS improves open-ended research agents by having model copies coordinate through task-specific workflows, then fine-tuning their shared model on selected orchestrator and subagent trajectories. After two cycles, it achieves 1.2–1.6 times the base model’s score per output token on four research benchmarks. This does not extend to coding benchmarks, where the reported ratios are 0.96 and 0.94.

hot.title: Long-WAM: Scaling the Context of World-Action Models
hot.summary: Long-WAM trains a robot controller to predict future video from visual history, then uses those predictions to generate actions. On RoboCasa GR-1, robot-domain autoregressive initialization raises success from 66.3% with 2.4 seconds of history to 78.7% with 19.2 seconds, while bidirectional initialization stays near 62%. This simulated comparison supports, but does not prove, the explanation that autoregressive pretraining helps use history.

hot.title: BrickBench: Evaluating Agentic Brick Design
hot.summary: BrickBench evaluates whether coding agents can turn written prompts into LEGO assemblies that meet construction checks and depict the requested scene. In BrickAgent, agents select parts, place them through compatible connectors, render builds, and revise them using validation feedback. GPT-6 Astra scores 1.00 on overall validity and 0.954 on VQA, but stability is simulated and does not establish real-world strength.

hot.title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
hot.summary: AgentGarten keeps game rules and changing state in executable code, while a shared neural renderer turns geometry into visual observations. Agents act from rendered views and refine multi-step tool use through play and written playbooks. In hide-and-seek, shelters appeared by round 4 and ramp crossings by round 10; these are experiment-specific results, not a controlled sample-efficiency comparison.

hot.title: Can Jev be Your Q or Policy in Reinforcement Learning?
hot.summary: The paper tests frozen Jev as guidance within reinforcement-learning training: as an action reference, exploration judge, and replay rater. Across nine MiniGrid tasks and three Atari games, learners sometimes outperform direct Jev control. Results depend on task and supplied information; in FourRooms, direct Jev succeeds in 96% of episodes with engineered navigation features, versus 40% without them.

hot.title: Prior or Feedback? What an LLM Uses When Adapting Neural Operators
hot.summary: The authors test LLM tuning of a Fourier neural operator (FNO) using hosted DeepSeek-V4 Pro over 20 trials. It achieves lower held-out test nRMSE in all 36 runs against random search and 35 of 36 against TPE. Its first proposal beats 91.7% of random configurations; replay shows choices respond to score assignments, but not that feedback improves test performance.

hot.title: RoboRSI: Stable, efficient, and reusable robot self-evolution in complex real-world environments
hot.summary: RoboRSI organizes robot tasks and capabilities into a skill hierarchy, uses execution evidence to localize failures, and validates bounded repairs before sharing them. On LIBERO-PRO, it achieves 297 of 600 successful valid episodes (49.5%), versus OpenETA’s 231 of 600 (38.5%), and covers 102 of 120 tasks. These results apply to the stated simulation protocol, not all physical settings.

hot.title: A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control
hot.summary: Success Guided Sampling (SGS) allocates training episodes across a fixed set of task configurations according to recent success rates, emphasizing situations with intermediate success while retaining nonzero sampling probability for all configurations. In settings, it improves results: Anymal-D locomotion reaches 73% success at 1 million environments, versus 54% with PLR. Hardware nut-and-bolt transfer succeeds in 18 of 48 trials.

hot.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
hot.summary: RoboJEPA predicts future visual features under robot actions and uses imagined outcomes to plan toward a goal image. Its predictor scales from 22 million to 8 billion parameters while keeping the V-JEPA 2.1 encoder fixed. A second-order compute law extrapolates held-out prediction error better than a standard power law, but does not establish a universal link to robot success.

hot.title: H-JEPA: End-to-End Learning of Hierarchical World Models for Visual Planning
hot.summary: H-JEPA plans visual tasks by learning three predictive levels, with each higher level predicting farther ahead in its own latent space and passing subgoals to finer planners. In a 50-task simulated AntMaze evaluation, three-level H-JEPA reaches 73.3% success, versus 18.0% for flat LeWM. A separate compute sweep shows a higher-success, lower-planner-compute frontier, not a wall-clock speedup; evidence is from simulation and offline DROID evaluation.

hot.title: NCM: Next-Concept Modeling: Fast, Parallel Coarse-to-Fine Text Generation
hot.summary: Diffusion language models (DLMs) offer parallel sampling for faster generation than autoregressive models, an increasingly important advantage as inference becomes a dominant computational workload. hot.title: Dino Forcing Flow Models: Do not denoise what you can predict
hot.summary: DINO Forcing uses a pretrained DINO vision encoder to guide image generation without separately denoising a feature stream. From a noisy image, it predicts DINO features and reuses them as conditioning, with feature alignment during training. On ImageNet, it reports unguided FID 2.47 after 100 latent-space epochs and 5.53 after 200 pixel-space epochs; these comparisons are benchmark-specific, not wall-clock evidence.

hot.title: Zatom-2: Multitask Pretraining on Atomistic Data for Generative Modeling across Domains
hot.summary: Zatom-2 tests whether atom-level pretraining on molecular and material data transfers to protein backbone generation. It uses shared atomic geometry and combines generation, structure prediction, and force-and-energy prediction, then finetunes on a small protein-domain dataset. On a computational designability test, its force-and-energy-prediction initialization reaches 74.80% for long proteins, versus 67.81% from scratch, but trails RFdiffusion3 on in-distribution proteins.

hot.title: SuperNav: An Agentic Navigation System for Any Task in Any Scene
hot.summary: SuperNav uses a pretrained multimodal large language model (MLLM) to navigate environments across single-object, ordered multi-object, and demand-driven tasks. A harness provides tools, reusable Skills, task state, and context management; the model selects destinations while an executor handles motion. On 150 Habitat-GS single-object tasks, its Geo-based Executor achieves 78.00% success versus UniNaVid's 34.00%, supporting the complete system only in tested settings.

hot.title: Multi-Agent Egocentric World Model with Fine-Grained Embodied Interaction
hot.summary: ME-World generates synchronized first-person videos as views of one evolving world. It conditions each stream on both agents’ motions and shared scene history, while jointly generating their video tokens. On the real benchmark, it scores 0.468 on environment consistency and 0.466 on state-update consistency, versus 0.421 and 0.413 for adapted MetaWorld. These scores measure cross-view feature agreement, not physical correctness.

hot.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
hot.summary: TokenRouter serves inference with per-token routing between language models, using asynchronous subservers and delayed batch admission. Developers define routing and state handoffs; each model server buffers arrivals and uses a throughput model to select a threshold. On R2R’s AIME setup at concurrency 4, it reports 244.56 generated tokens/s versus 89.62 for official R2R, a serving-efficiency result under routing assumptions.

hot.title: Connected Self Forcing: Beyond Local Learning in Video Autoregression
hot.summary: Connected Self Forcing (CSF) trains autoregressive video generation by replaying computations so later chunks can send gradients through earlier cached context to its generator. It supplements direct chunk supervision without retaining the full rollout graph or changing inference. With teacher-forcing initialization, CSF scores 0.8701 on 240-second chunk-wise generation, versus 0.8545 for Self Forcing; its Dynamic Degree is lower than both baselines.

hot.title: Cross-Embodiment Robot Foundation World Models with Latent Actions
hot.summary: LAC-WM learns a shared motion representation from human and robot observations, then projects a new robot’s actions into it so a pretrained world model can predict outcomes. In simulated dexterous pick-and-place, it reaches 22% success versus 15% for the explicit-action baseline, a 46.7% relative gain. On modified LIBERO, it scores 92.0% versus 82.4%; these are simulated results, with no hardware demonstration.

likes.title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
likes.summary: The authors train looped language models for terminal-state prediction and KV-cache sharing. A learned depth prior allocates supervision across recurrence counts, while orthogonal input injection preserves the injected signal. At 1.6B parameters and five recurrences, the model uses four terminal KV banks and matches a full-cache fixed-depth model’s seven-task average, 60.00% versus 59.90%. The study uses one seed per configuration.

likes.title: LiFT: Loop Flow Transformers
likes.summary: LiFT uses a shared transformer core within each diffusion step, training passes to refine velocity estimates along a correction path. On class-conditional ImageNet-1k at 256×256, LiFT-L/2 R10 run with eight loops and 50 steps reaches FID 10.95 at 28.24 TFLOPs per image, versus dense DiT-XL/2 with 250 steps at FID 14.30. This unguided, cross-scale comparison does not establish latency savings or generalization.

likes.title: Base Models Can Reason By Taking a Cue From Training Data
likes.summary: The authors test whether short fixed openings can elicit reasoning from language models without changing their weights. On MATH-500, Olmo-3-7B pass@1 rises from 42% without a cue to 78% with “Okay,” versus 75% after reinforcement learning. In a controlled data-edit experiment, renaming “okay” to “chicken” makes “Chicken” effective, supporting cue effects in these tested settings, not all models.

likes.title: Introducing Beam: Reflection’s 501B open-weight model
likes.summary: Reflection introduces Beam, its first open-weight model: a sparse Mixture-of-Experts with 501 billion total and 23 billion active parameters, aimed at coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. It was pretrained on 23.8 trillion curated tokens and then trained with a high-compute reinforcement learning run of over 100 million rollouts on 10.5K NVIDIA GB300 GPUs. Beam is competitive with larger open models while using far less inference compute, and its weights are slated for release under Apache 2.0 later in the month.

likes.title: Truly Subquadratic 3SUM and Truly Subcubic APSP via Triangles in Sparse Lopsided Graphs
likes.summary: The authors introduce a deterministic algorithm that computes selected entries of a thin matrix product without computing the full product or each entry separately. It recursively multiplies rectangular matrices and prunes work for unrequested outputs. It gives 3SUM in O(n^1.9992) and directed APSP in O(n^2.9995) for polynomially bounded integers in the word-RAM model, asymptotic bounds rather than measured speedups.

likes.title: UndoBench: Separating Task Competence from Recovery Capability in Tool-Using AI Agents
likes.summary: The authors introduce UndoBench to evaluate whether AI agents recover safely when external operations fail. It pairs identical-seed control and faulted runs, measuring recovery only when the control succeeds, and records external effects. Across 12 held-out workflows, control success was 83.54%, but conditional recovery was 46.72%; results cover sandboxed trials with one lost acknowledgment fault.

likes.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign European Model on the Pareto Frontier
likes.summary: Kolibri is an open-weight bilingual model designed for local deployment on controlled infrastructure. It activates 3.46B of 78.1B parameters per token and uses sliding-window attention in 40 of 50 blocks, with full attention in every fifth block. Against Kolibri Origin, its post-trained scores are higher in English and German, with 2.7× reported decode throughput under the paper’s measurement setup.

likes.title: QF3: Fast Flow RL with Filtered Q-Gradients
likes.summary: QF3 addresses robot learning by improving flow policies from replayed experience. It anchors policy updates to replay actions through flow matching, then applies a critic gradient to a one-step action prediction, clipping velocity corrections that stray too far from the replay target. In tested settings, clipping prevents collapse; on G1 dance tracking, training reaches full episodes about 10 times faster than FPO++.

likes.title: Level-of-Token Diffusion
likes.summary: LoT allocates image and video transformer tokens according to desired detail, using larger patches in simple regions and smaller patches where detail matters. A transformer processes the shorter sequence, while extent-aware flow recovery produces a full-resolution denoising field. At matched 2× video token budget, LoT reports 2.262× speedup and higher Aesthetic and Imaging scores than Foveated Diffusion, but not higher Dynamic Degree at the highest tested compression.

likes.title: Kernel Autoresearch for Open-Ended Model Discovery
likes.summary: KERNAUT uses language-model coding agents to discover reusable Gaussian-process kernels as programs, while a trusted interpreter assembles proposals through positive-semidefinite-preserving constructions. Across several benchmarks, selected kernels improved on fixed or learned references in some settings—including an 8.3% mean test-CRPS reduction in black-box optimization campaigns and a strong enzyme-kinetics result—though benefits varied by task and were not universal.

likes.title: OpenWAM: An Open Framework for Composable World-Action Models
likes.summary: OpenWAM tests links between video predictions and robot actions, including reuse of action models. It compares generation routes in a shared framework and trains separate dynamics models on demonstrations and counterfactual transitions. After target-task video adaptation, a frozen local-context inverse dynamics model achieves 84.0% mean closed-loop success across four held-out LIBERO-90 simulation targets, versus 47.0% for full-context conditioning.

likes.title: RSIGym: A Flexible Environment for Recursive Self-Improvement
likes.summary: RSIGym provides reusable services for training, inference, rollouts, evaluation, and sandbox computation, while permissions let agents change data, training settings, harnesses, or combinations. In one budgeted run, six agents improved 29 of 30 settings across five benchmarks. Opus 5 achieved an RSI-Index of 0.4809 and raised SWE-bench Verified from 17.67% to 50.33%. The results do not establish progress across later cycles.

likes.title: Video Prediction Policy 2: Predict Better, Act Better
likes.summary: VPP2 trains a video model on manipulation events with detailed captions, then distills it for fixed-horizon prediction and conditions an action expert on predicted futures. It evaluates instruction-following and robot manipulation. On ALOHA, it averages 58.5% success across 10 task categories, versus 40.0% for π0.5 and 20.5% for Fast-WAM, leading in 9 categories without task-specific fine-tuning on the represented embodiment.

likes.title: Navier-Stokes lost in translation: Why Lean verification of AI autoformalisation does not guarantee correct natural language proofs
likes.summary: The paper examines whether Lean formalizations preserve natural-language proofs. Lean checks proofs against encoded statements, but compilation does not verify that translation preserves the source. Comparing OpenAI’s Navier–Stokes paper with its Lean formalization, the authors find an estimate requiring five rather than four extra derivatives, concluding the formalization is not faithful, not that the natural-language proof is wrong.

likes.title: A Call for an Open Tokenizer Benchmark
likes.summary: Cognetta proposes a public benchmark for comparing text tokenizers by training language models under shared rules and scoring prediction loss in bits per byte of original text. The design fixes most model and training choices while allowing tokenizer-dependent vocabulary sizes. Bits-per-byte scores each tokenizer’s canonical segmentation. The paper reports no benchmark results or validated predictive metrics, and leaves batching unresolved.
